toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: no libgloss at all -- vplat_syscalls.c provides every stub newlib
# needs, so only -lc/-lgcc remain.
VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c
VPLAT_LIBS      := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share test.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T test.ld $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing hsim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/hsim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/hsim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share hsim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: no libgloss at all -- vplat_syscalls.c provides every stub newlib
# needs, so only -lc/-lgcc remain.
VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c
VPLAT_LIBS      := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share hsim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (hsim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T $(LDSCRIPT) $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: one ELF built against the vplat runtime (UART stdio +
# SimControl exit, NO libgloss_vh / semihosting) runs to completion on the
# cycle-accurate engine from reset: it prints via the modeled UART and
# terminates the simulation with exit code 0 via the SimControl write.
#
# This is the leg that is impossible with an -mvh build (vsim has no
# semihosting; see docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Nonzero exit code must propagate through vsim too.
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_exit41.elf >/dev/null || fail "exit41 build failed"
timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 41 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 41"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andes-sim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andes-sim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andes-sim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep -q ' T _start' || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" | grep -q ' T _write' \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandes_sim_runtime.a" | grep -q ' T m_trap_entry' \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andes-sim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landes_sim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Build the user-facing andes-sim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandes_sim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andes-sim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andes-sim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ar

OUT ?= ../build/runtime

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V
# arch attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andes-sim.ld

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andes-sim.ld: andes-sim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

# runs printf -- the bytes go out the MODELED UART, cycle-accurately --
# and drains at vplat_roi_end. Asserts all three: the hello text (from the

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F3 contract: the whole link recipe collapses into two flags --
#
#   gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
#       -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf
#
# The specs file swaps the startfile to our crt0.o, appends -T andes-sim.ld
# and rewrites the library sequence to
# `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group` (no -lgloss,
# no semihosting). The produced ELF must run on all three engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/hello.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello from specs\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl vplat_roi_end\nvplat_roi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# The two-flag user command (plus a link map for the no-gloss assert).
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andes-sim.specs "$TMP/hello.c" -o "$TMP/hello.elf" \
  -Wl,-Map,"$TMP/hello.map" || fail "two-flag specs link failed"

grep 'libandes_sim_runtime\.a' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null \
  || fail "link map does not pull libandes_sim_runtime.a"
if grep 'gloss' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null; then
  fail "link map pulls a libgloss (semihosting leaked into the link)"
fi

# cycle
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# fast
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --model fast "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "fast: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# hybrid (pc trigger on the same symbols a user would publish)
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger pc \
        --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end \
        "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from specs' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing 'hello from specs' in: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[pc window_cycles\] [0-9]+' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Build the user-facing andes-sim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandes_sim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andes-sim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andes-sim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ar

OUT ?= ../build/runtime

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V
# arch attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andes-sim.ld

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andes-sim.ld: andes-sim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif

LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: no libgloss at all -- vplat_syscalls.c provides every stub newlib
# needs, so only -lc/-lgcc remain.
VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c
VPLAT_LIBS      := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andes-sim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andes-sim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andes-sim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: built THROUGH the shipped runtime library with the same two-flag
# command users type (-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the
# suites regression-test the real artifact. No libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs.
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T $(LDSCRIPT) $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F2: `./hsim build [--what TARGET] --dry-run`.
#
# --dry-run must print the underlying commands without executing them.
# This lets us unit-test the build subparser quickly (the real build
# takes ~5 min and is exercised by F6 verification).

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"

# 1. Default (no --what): dry-run lists ALL the underlying steps:
#    bash setup.sh + make -C tests/fixtures.
out=$("$HSIM" build --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "build --dry-run exit nonzero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "bash .*setup\.sh"          || fail "missing setup.sh line:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "make .*-C .*tests/fixtures" || fail "missing tests/fixtures line:\n$out"
ok "build --dry-run lists setup.sh and tests/fixtures"

# 2. --what qemu: dry-run lists ONLY the qemu builder, not vsim/plugin/simpoint/fixtures.
out=$("$HSIM" build --what qemu --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "build --what qemu --dry-run exit nonzero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "build_qemu\.sh"           || fail "missing build_qemu.sh:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "build_vsim\.sh"           && fail "should NOT list vsim:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "build_simpoint\.sh"       && fail "should NOT list simpoint:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "tests/fixtures"           && fail "should NOT list fixtures:\n$out"
ok "build --what qemu --dry-run lists only qemu"

# 3. --what fixtures: only the make line.
out=$("$HSIM" build --what fixtures --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "build --what fixtures --dry-run exit nonzero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "make .*-C .*tests/fixtures" || fail "missing tests/fixtures line:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "setup\.sh"                  && fail "should NOT list setup.sh:\n$out"
ok "build --what fixtures --dry-run lists only fixtures"

set +e
out=$("$HSIM" build --what bogus --dry-run 2>&1)
rc=$?

ok "build --what bogus exits non-zero (rc=$rc)"

diff -q <(git -C "$ROOT" show HEAD:setup.sh) "$ROOT/setup.sh" >/dev/null \
  || fail "setup.sh differs from HEAD (must be unchanged)"
ok "setup.sh unchanged from HEAD"

echo "PASS test_hsim_build_dry"

#
# Runs the same args through the Python golden (hsim) and the C++ driver
# (build/andes-sim), then diffs stdout+stderr and the exit code. As each
# later feature ports a subcommand, it adds its cases below; a green parity
# run is the evidence the C++ path matches the reference it replaces.
#
# F0 ships the harness skeleton with zero cases, so it exits 0 vacuously.
# Override the two binaries via the GOLDEN / NEW env vars if needed.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

GOLDEN="${GOLDEN:-$ROOT/hsim}"        # Python reference driver
NEW="${NEW:-$ROOT/build/andes-sim}"   # C++ driver under test

# everything), so run the C++ driver in dev mode -- e.g. so the dev-only
# `list fixtures` target resolves on both sides.

pass=0
fail=0

# compare <case-name> -- <args...>
# Invoke GOLDEN and NEW with identical args; require matching stdout+stderr
# and exit code. Records a pass/fail; never aborts so all cases report.

960	  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
961	  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
962	  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
963	    `csrwi 0x7C0,1` PC from CsrTrigger (csr mode)
964	  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
965	    close on first retire of end_pc).
966	
967	---
968	
969	## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)
970	
971	Fixtures linked with `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting) can print only where a QEMU
972	intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no semihosting, which is
973	why the Phase-2 "no syscalls inside the ROI" rule exists. The **vplat
974	runtime** removes the per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
975	(`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
976	engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
977	and across a `hybrid` handoff.
978	
979	| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
980	|---------|--------|------------------|------|
981	| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
982	| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
983	| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |
984	
985	Build (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`):
986	
987	```sh
988	"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" \
989	  -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
990	  -Itests/fixtures/runtime -Wall -T tests/fixtures/test.ld \
991	  tests/fixtures/runtime/crt0.S tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S \
992	  tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c \
993	  your_prog.c -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group -o your_prog.elf
994	```
995	
996	Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
997	(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io). Per-feature smoke
998	tests live in `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f4.sh`.
999	
1000	Notes:
1001	
1002	- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
1003	  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
1004	  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
1005	- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
1006	  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
1007	  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
1008	  stat writeback).
1009	- **Do NOT compile the csr ROI markers into vplat binaries.** CSR `0x7C0` is
1010	  MILMB on the Andes core; the exit marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) enables ILM at
1011	  base 0 and shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run (the program dies in an
1012	  illegal-instruction trap loop). Hybrid runs only survive it because the
1013	  exit marker retires on vsim. Delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use

scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `csrwi 0x7C0,1` PC from CsrTrigger (csr mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

---

## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

Fixtures linked with `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting) can print only where a QEMU
intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no semihosting, which is
why the Phase-2 "no syscalls inside the ROI" rule exists. The **vplat
runtime** removes the per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

Build (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" \
  -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -Itests/fixtures/runtime -Wall -T tests/fixtures/test.ld \
  tests/fixtures/runtime/crt0.S tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S \
  tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c \
  your_prog.c -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group -o your_prog.elf
```

Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io). Per-feature smoke
tests live in `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f4.sh`.

Notes:

- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
  stat writeback).
- **Do NOT compile the csr ROI markers into vplat binaries.** CSR `0x7C0` is
  MILMB on the Andes core; the exit marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) enables ILM at
  base 0 and shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run (the program dies in an
  illegal-instruction trap loop). Hybrid runs only survive it because the
  exit marker retires on vsim. Delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use
  `--trigger pc` instead (see `tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c`:
  `say_hello` / `vplat_roi_end`).
- A `printf` inside the measured window now works (the UART is modeled and
  its MMIO cost is real), but it still adds those UART cycles to the figure -
  keep measured kernels I/O-free when you care about clean numbers.
- `docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb` sections 2, 3 and 4d run the same
  `hello.elf` through all three models.

---

## 6. Running the full test suite

After any change to the simulator or plugin, run the suite:

```sh
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

`JOBS=8` is the practical cap on this 128-core host (vsim Verilator
processes are CPU-hungry; the default cap of 128 saturates the box and
times out). Logs go to `/tmp/e2e-<RAND>/`; failed-test logs are

The runtime ships prebuilt as `libandes_sim_runtime.a`. Build it once
(`./hsim build --what runtime`, or any fixture build does it implicitly),
then compile with two extra flags (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`,
no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

`-B` points gcc at the built artifacts (use the absolute path to
`<repo>/build/runtime` when compiling outside the repo);
`-specs=andes-sim.specs` swaps the startfile to the runtime's `crt0.o`,
adds `-T andes-sim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and rewrites the library
list to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`, so no
libgloss or semihosting can leak into the link.

Without the gcc driver (a custom build system), link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andes-sim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

Sources live in `runtime/` (crt0.S boot, trap.S + handler.c trap
diagnostics, vplat_syscalls.c newlib stubs). `crt0.o` is shipped next to
the archive, not inside it: nothing references `_start`, so the linker
would never extract it from a `.a`.

Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io); they are built
with exactly the two-flag command above. Per-feature smoke tests live in
`tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f9.sh`.

content.content:
## 2. Build ONE program for every engine

`fast` runs an ELF on QEMU alone - a **transparent passthrough**: the program's
own input/output flows straight through and QEMU's exit code is propagated.

Historically you needed a different build per engine: QEMU wanted `-mvh`
(semihosting), which vsim cannot service. This repo now ships a portable
runtime - the **vplat runtime** (`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) -
that talks only to devices BOTH engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Device | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550 @ `0xf0300000`  | yes | yes |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000`   | yes | yes |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF command @ `0xe0080010` | yes | yes |

No semihosting and no "which engine am I on" probe (a hybrid run migrates the
process between engines mid-run, so any boot-time detection would go stale) -
one binary therefore runs on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid`
handoff.

The build: your C file plus the fixture runtime (`crt0.S`, `trap.S`,
`handler.c`, `vplat_syscalls.c`) and the `test.ld` linker script (load base
`0x00100000`, valid RAM on both engines), with `-nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs`
and plain `-lc -lgcc` (no `-lgloss_vh`). The `say_hello` function and the
`roi_end` label delimit the region section 4d will measure.
=== CELL 13 ===
%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null     # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (also done by `source ./setup.sh`)
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "toolchain missing - run: source ./setup.sh"; exit 1; }

cat > hello.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  /* ROI end marker for hybrid --pc-end: the return point after the call. */
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl roi_end\nroi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# vplat runtime: UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io; no -mvh.
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -Itests/fixtures/runtime -Wall -T tests/fixtures/test.ld \
  tests/fixtures/runtime/crt0.S tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S \
  tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c \
  hello.c -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group -o hello.elf

echo "built hello.elf:"; file hello.elf
=== CELL 13 OUTPUTS ===
built hello.elf:
hello.elf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, UCB RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, not stripped

Done. All 6 features implemented, committed, and green. The user command is now:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf
```

Per your rename request, everything is branded **andes-sim** (no "hsim" in any new artifact): `libandes_sim_runtime.a`, `andes-sim.specs`, `andes-sim.ld`, roadmap `andes_sim_runtime_lib.md`.

What shipped (one commit per feature):

- `632cecf` **F1 (structural)**: runtime sources moved from `tests/fixtures/runtime/` to top-level `runtime/`; `test.ld` became `runtime/andes-sim.ld`. `rt_c_helpers.h` (csr markers, not portable) stayed test-side.
- `1f4e969` **F2**: `make -C runtime` builds `build/runtime/{libandes_sim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andes-sim.ld}`. `crt0.o` ships next to the archive because the linker never extracts `_start` from a `.a`.
- `a75e32d` **F3**: `andes-sim.specs` - swaps in our crt0, adds `-T andes-sim.ld`, rewrites libs to `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`; the link map proves no libgloss/semihosting leaks in.
- `3d2ee53` **F4**: vplat fixtures now build with the exact two-flag user command, so e2e regression-tests the shipped artifact.
- `cdcce5a` **F5**: `build --what runtime` on both drivers (golden `hsim` + `andes-sim`, byte-parity). `build` all needs no new step - the fixtures Makefile self-builds the lib.
- `25c0dbc` **F6**: USER_GUIDE section 5 + tutorial rewritten; all hello.elf cells re-executed with real outputs (cycle 3640 cycles, hybrid window 14668 - layout shifted slightly with archive link order).

Final validation, all passing: e2e 35/35, vplat smoke f1-f9, parity 9/9. One fix along the way: a test pipeline bug where `grep -q` + `pipefail` turned a successful match into a SIGPIPE failure - the new tests use `grep >/dev/null` instead.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F14 name-swap contract (driver/ROADMAP.md): the user-facing entry is
# `./andes-sim` (the C++ driver, self-building); the Python golden is
# retired to `hsim.py` (reference only, prog name and behavior frozen);
# the bare `hsim` name no longer exists; the parity harness still finds
# its golden via the new default path.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# 1. the hsim name is retired; the golden lives at hsim.py.
[ -e "$ROOT/hsim" ] && fail "repo-root 'hsim' still exists (name not retired)"
[ -x "$ROOT/hsim.py" ] || fail "golden hsim.py missing or not executable"

# 2. ./andes-sim works from the repo root (and self-builds if needed).
[ -x "$ROOT/andes-sim" ] || fail "repo-root andes-sim entry missing"
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && ./andes-sim list models 2>&1) || fail "./andes-sim list models failed: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hybrid' || fail "list models lacks hybrid: $out"

# 3. the golden still answers (frozen reference) and keeps its prog name.
out=$("$ROOT/hsim.py" build --dry-run 2>&1) || fail "hsim.py build --dry-run failed: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'setup.sh' || fail "golden dry-run misses setup.sh: $out"

# 4. parity harness default GOLDEN points at hsim.py (no env override).
ANDES_SIM_DEV=1 bash "$ROOT/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "parity.sh fails with its default GOLDEN after the rename"

ok "F14 cutover: ./andes-sim is the entry, hsim.py is the golden"

# RED test: the `demo` subcommand and `list demos` choice are removed.

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"

cd "$ROOT"

# 1. ./hsim demo <anything> -> argparse rejects the subcommand.
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" demo T1 2>&1); rc=$?

set +e

## 0.5 Quick start with `./hsim`

`./hsim` is the canonical end-user entry point. It wraps the
developer-grade scripts documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`,
`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind four subcommands.

Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:

```sh
./hsim build                                            # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
./hsim list fixtures                                    # discover available fixtures
./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr     # one CSR-mode handoff
./hsim test                                             # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
```

Expected last line of `./hsim test`:

```
PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
```

Subcommand cheat sheet:

| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one handoff end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is two legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./andes-sim`
35	
36	`./andes-sim` is the canonical end-user entry point (the C++ driver; it
37	self-builds on first use). It wraps the developer-grade scripts
38	documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`, `tests/e2e.sh`,
39	`scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind a few subcommands.
40	
41	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
42	
43	```sh
44	./andes-sim build                                       # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
45	./andes-sim list engines                                # discover the built engines
46	./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
47	  tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf                         # one CSR-trigger handoff
48	./andes-sim test                                        # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
49	```
50	
51	Expected last line of `./andes-sim test`:
52	
53	```
54	PASS 45, FAIL 0, SKIP 0 (elapsed: <Ns>)
55	```
56	
57	Subcommand cheat sheet:
58	
59	| Command                                                          | What it does                                                        |
60	|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
61	| `./andes-sim list <models|engines>`                              | List the 3 models or the discovered engines.                       |
62	| `./andes-sim build [--what TARGET] [--dry-run]`                  | Build artifacts; targets: `all`, `qemu`, `vsim`, `plugin`, `simpoint`, `fixtures`, `runtime`. |
63	| `./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger csr|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>` | Run one ELF on a model (hybrid = QEMU -> vsim handoff). |
64	| `./andes-sim test [--filter REGEX] [--model hybrid --trigger csr --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium|pc|both] [--jobs N]` | Run the e2e suite; defaults `--mode both --jobs 8`.              |
65	
66	Run `./andes-sim <cmd> -h` for the full flag list of a subcommand (set
67	`ANDES_SIM_DEV=1` to see the developer commands). The SimPoint pipeline
68	(`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`,
69	`replay`) still lives in the Python reference driver `./hsim.py` until
70	the C++ port lands. The rest of this guide (Sections 1-7) documents the
71	underlying scripts and is useful when you need to bypass `./andes-sim`
72	(custom env vars, single-leg debugging, alternative CPU YAML, etc.).
73	
74	---
75	
76	## 1. Build and environment setup
77	
78	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
79	
80	Install these on the host once:
81	
82	| Package          | Notes                                                |
83	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
84	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
85	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
86	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
87	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
88	| `python3`        | orchestrator, plugin tests                           |
89	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
90	| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
91	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
92	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
93	| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
94	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
95	
96	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
97	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
98	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
99	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
100	
101	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
102	
103	```sh
104	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
105	cd hybrid_sim
106	```
107	
108	If you forgot `--recursive`:
109	
110	```sh
111	git submodule update --init --recursive
112	```
113	
114	Submodules under this repo:
115	
116	| Path             | What it is                                          |
117	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
118	| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
119	| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
120	| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |
121	
122	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
123	
124	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
125	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
126	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
127	
128	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
129	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
130	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
131	`config.env`:
132	
133	```sh
134	# config.env
135	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
136	```
137	
138	The single variable today is:
139

Done - committed as `cd86036`. The `hsim` name is retired:

- **`./andes-sim`** is now the repo-root entry: a small wrapper that self-builds `build/andes-sim` on first use, so a fresh clone can run it directly (verified by deleting the binary and re-running).

- **Tests**: every `GOLDEN`/`HSIM` path now points at `hsim.py` (parity.sh default, tests/andes_sim, tests/hsim, the top-level mode tests).
- **Docs translated, not just renamed**: `./hsim run <elf> --mode csr` became `./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger csr --engine vsim:<cpu> <elf>` (I verified the C++ accepts ELF-first ordering and ran a translated icount example end-to-end: PASS, 13182 window cycles). The SimPoint pipeline (`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`, `archive`, `replay`) does not exist in the C++ driver yet, so USER_GUIDE/tutorial deliberately reference those as `./hsim.py ...` with a "until the C++ port lands" note. `HSIM_MMAP_DIR` keeps its name - it is a live env var both drivers read (`driver/shm.cpp:85`), not a name reference.

Validation: cutover test, parity 9/9, golden's own tests (`build_dry`, `list`), runtime-target, f1/f4, and vplat f6 all pass. Your uncommitted work (driver/cmd_list.cpp, main.cpp, models.hpp, the f2/release-surface tests, parity.sh dev-mode export) is untouched and still unstaged - I temporarily set aside the two overlapping files and reapplied your diff cleanly after committing.

Not included (the rest of roadmap F14, beyond the rename): wiring `build_driver.sh` into `setup.sh`, `build --what driver`, migrating `tests/hsim/` into `tests/andes_sim/`, and the `engine_interface.md` author guide.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	**Primary path (`./andes-sim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
20	first use), used in all user-facing docs. The retired Python driver is kept
21	as `hsim.py`, the byte-parity golden (`tests/andes_sim/parity.sh`); the
22	SimPoint pipeline (`run --mode simpoint`, `estimate`, `profile`, `cluster`,
23	`archive`, `replay`) still runs only there until the C++ port lands.
24	
25	```sh
26	./andes-sim build                  # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
27	./andes-sim test                   # full e2e suite (defaults: MODE=both, JOBS=8)
28	./andes-sim run --model fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger csr|pc|icount] [--engine ID] <elf>
29	./andes-sim list <models|engines>
30	```
31	
32	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
33	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
34	
35	```sh
36	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
37	source ./setup.sh
38	
39	# Build individual components
40	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
41	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
42	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT="$PWD/QEMU"  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree); QEMU_ROOT must be absolute (make -C chdirs first)
43	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
44	
45	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
46	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
47	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
48	
49	# Clean
50	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
51	```
52	
53	**Outputs:**
54	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
55	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
56	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
57	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
58	
59	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
60	
61	## Running Tests
62	
63	```sh
64	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
65	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
66	
67	# Run with specific options
68	JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
69	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
70	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
71	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
72	
73	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
74	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
75	# To run ctest directly after build:
76	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
77	```
78	
79	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
80	
81	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
82	
83	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver (parity vs the golden + feature contracts); `tests/hsim/test_hsim_*.sh` are the retired golden's own per-feature smoke tests (they now invoke `hsim.py`). Both families run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
84	
85	## Architecture
86	
87	### Two-Phase Handoff
88	
89	```
90	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
91	```
92	
93	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
94	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
95	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
96	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
97	
98	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but with the QEMU2 leg removed those extra CSRs are no longer restored anywhere -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
99	
100	### Trigger Modes
101	
102	The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.
103	
104	Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
105	- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
106	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
107	
108	Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
109	- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for CSR-less workloads.
110	- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.
111	
112	`./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger csr|pc|icount` is the unified orchestrator (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` for SimPoint); `tests/e2e.sh` drives csr/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.
113	
114	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
115

   3. "design a runtime library that contains all of those files so that users could link with -lhsim_runtime. The point is to simplify the user's compilation command." Followed by the user pasting the current long compile command ("$GCC" ... 4 runtime sources + test.ld + --start-group ...) saying "the current command is to complicated for users to use".
   4. "implement it" — implement the 6-feature roadmap (andes_sim_runtime_lib.md).
   5. "rename hsim as andes-sim" (mid-implementation) — brand all new artifacts andes-sim instead of hsim.
   6. "rename the hsim golden driver and ./hsim references to andes-sim too" — the F14 cutover from driver/ROADMAP.md: repo-root ./andes-sim = C++ driver entry, Python golden moves to hsim.py, sweep all references.
   7. "commit" — commit the user's remaining in-flight working-tree changes (release-surface driver work + remove_qemu2.md deletion).
   User's standing global rules (from ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md): TDD hard gate (failing test before any non-test edit; state RED/GREEN/REFACTOR phase), Tidy First (structural vs behavioral commits separated), simple English (ESL learner), ASCII only (no em dashes/smart quotes), answer on line 1, no preamble, token efficiency, never speculate about unread code, roadmap as task-named .md in repo root, don't clobber top-level ROADMAP.md, commit messages end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (fast/functional) + vsim (Verilator/SystemC, cycle) two-phase handoff; cycle figure = vsim mcycle delta; no QEMU2 leg.
   - vplat device ABI: UART2 16550 @0xf0300020/0xf0300034, SimControl exit @0xe0080000, HTIF file-io magicmem @0xe0080010 — one ELF runs on fast/cycle/hybrid.
   - Bare-metal runtime: crt0.S (caches, sp/gp, mstatus.FS/VS, bss clear, calls init_mtvec/main/_exit; non-zero harts write SKIPPED 0x01234571), trap.S (m_trap_entry saves 31 regs + mepc/mstatus/mxstatus, calls handle_trap, mret; RISC-V .align 6 emits R_RISCV_ALIGN reloc so pre-link offset 0x3e is normal), handler.c (init_mtvec constructor, fatal-trap diagnostics).
   - Library packaging: crt0.o must ship OUTSIDE the .a (nothing references _start so the linker never extracts it); archive pull-chain crt0→init_mtvec/_exit→handler.o+vplat_syscalls.o→m_trap_entry→trap.o.
   - GCC specs files: %rename link, `-T andes-sim.ld%s` (%s resolves via startfile prefixes), *startfile crt0%O%s, empty *endfile, *lib `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group`; spec files do NOT support comments; -B provides startfile prefixes + -L + specs lookup.
   - rv64gc runtime objects link into rv64gcv programs (ld unions RISC-V arch attributes).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F5 contract: `build --what runtime` builds the user-facing
# runtime library (build/runtime/: libandes_sim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
# andes-sim.ld, andes-sim.specs) on BOTH drivers, byte-parity included.
#
# `build` (all) needs no new step: the fixtures Makefile self-builds the
# runtime through its grouped target, so the lib arrives transitively. The
# explicit target exists for users who want the library WITHOUT building
# the fixture ELFs.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
GOLDEN="$ROOT/hsim.py"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. dry-run: golden and new agree byte-for-byte and name the runtime make.
g=$(cd "$ROOT" && "$GOLDEN" build --what runtime --dry-run 2>&1); grc=$?
n=$(cd "$ROOT" && "$BIN" build --what runtime --dry-run 2>&1);    nrc=$?
[ "$grc" = "0" ] || fail "golden build --what runtime rc=$grc: $g"
[ "$grc" = "$nrc" ] || fail "rc differs: golden=$grc new=$nrc"
[ "$g" = "$n" ] || {
  diff <(printf '%s\n' "$g") <(printf '%s\n' "$n") >&2
  fail "build --what runtime dry-run output differs from golden"
}
printf '%s\n' "$n" | grep -q 'make -C runtime' \
  || fail "dry-run does not delegate to make -C runtime: $n"

# 2. real run produces the artifacts.
rm -rf "$ROOT/build/runtime"
out=$(cd "$ROOT" && "$BIN" build --what runtime 2>&1); rc=$?
[ "$rc" = "0" ] || fail "real build --what runtime failed (rc=$rc): $out"
for a in libandes_sim_runtime.a crt0.o andes-sim.ld andes-sim.specs; do
  [ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/$a" ] || fail "missing build/runtime/$a"
done

ok "F5 build --what runtime (parity + artifacts)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# andes-sim: repo-root entry for the C++ driver (build/andes-sim).
# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andes-sim
# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
exec "$BIN" "$@"

 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *

 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */

 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or

 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is

 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
