# roi_markers.md - portable ROI markers + IDE line anchors

## Problem

1. The in-binary ROI markers are `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on
   the Andes core: the exit marker enables ILM at base 0 and kills any
   standalone run (`--model fast` trap loop). So today one binary cannot
   carry markers AND run on all engines.
2. Users want to pick the ROI like setting two breakpoints in an IDE:
   click a line, the IDE knows `file.c:42`, the tool does the rest. Today
   the only external anchors are symbol names or raw `0x` addresses.

## Design (one mechanism, three front-ends)

Both engines already reduce every trigger to a PC watch:
- vsim: `csr_trigger.hpp` pre-scans the code bytes for marker encodings
  and builds a pc->kind map; PC mode injects via `add_pc_hit()`.
- QEMU plugin: matches the marker encoding at translate time, or takes
  `enter_pc=0x...`.

So the engine layer stays untouched. ROI = a pair of PCs. What changes is
how the pair gets named:

| Front-end          | Source                                  | Status |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------|
| in-binary markers  | HINT NOP pair (was: csrwi 0x7C0)        | F2/F3  |
| symbol / 0xaddr    | `--pc-start S --pc-end E`               | exists |
| file:line (IDE)    | `--pc-start main.c:42` via DWARF        | F4     |

### Marker fix: RISC-V HINT pair

Integer-computational instructions with rd=x0 are architectural NOPs on
every conforming RISC-V core (spec "HINT" space). Candidate encodings:

- ENTER:   `slti x0, x0, IMM_ENTER`   (OP-IMM, rd=0, 12-bit payload)
- EXIT:    `slti x0, x0, IMM_EXIT`
- RUNTIME: `slt  x0, rs1, x0`         (R-type, rd=0; kind read from rs1
                                       at retire, same as today's
                                       `csrw 0x7C0, rs1`)

Properties: true NOP on fast, cycle, hybrid AND real silicon (MILMB
hazard gone, the docs' "never run marker binaries standalone" warning is
deleted); `slti`/`slt` have no compressed form, so the plugin `sz==4`
gate and the vsim 16/32 scanner invariant hold unchanged.

F2 must verify the exact imm values against the unpriv spec HINT table
and must not collide with allocated standard hints (Zihintntl uses
`add x0, x0, x2..x5`; Zihintpause uses a FENCE form) or Andes extensions.

### IDE anchors: file:line -> PC

`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` learn a third form, `path.c:NN`:
- Resolve via the DWARF line table (v1: shell out to toolchain
  `objdump --dwarf=decodedline`; toolchain is already a doctor-checked
  dependency). Pick the lowest `is_stmt` address for the exact line.
- If the line has no code (optimized out), snap forward to the next line
  that has code, gdb-style, and PRINT the snap.
- Always echo the resolution: `main.c:42 -> 0x80000124 (matmul+0x18)`.
- Requires `-g` in the user's compile flags (no codegen impact; add to
  the documented two-flag command).

Known limits (same as any debugger breakpoint, document them):
- first-hit semantics in loops (same as today's pc mode),
- at -O2 a line can map to several PCs or move; for tight attribution
  the existing advice holds (anchor on calls / memory ops).

IDE contract is then trivial and editor-agnostic: gutter click ->
`file:line` -> `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc
--pc-start A.c:10 --pc-end A.c:20 app.elf` -> cycle figure back.

## Features

### F1: trigger-rename (structural)
Rename the user surface `--trigger csr` -> `--trigger marker` (the name
is wrong even today: vsim never executes it as a CSR, it PC-watches).
No alias kept (pre-release). e2e `MODE=csr` -> `MODE=marker`.
- Key files: driver/{cli.cpp, main.cpp, cmd_run.cpp, hybrid.cpp,
  run_plan.cpp, engine_registry.cpp, models.hpp, *_test.cpp}, hsim.py
  (lockstep, parity), tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh,
  tests/andes_sim/*, tests/hsim/*, docs/USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md.
- Deps: none. Pure rename commit (Tidy First), behavior unchanged.
- State: todo

### F2: hint-encoding (behavioral)
Rewrite `hybrid_match_handoff_insn` for the HINT encodings (remove the
CSR form entirely). Update the inverse encoders + doctest first (RED).
- Key files: include/hybrid/insn_match.h,
  verilator/tests/hybrid/{insn_match.test.cpp, insn_encoders.hpp,
  csr_trigger.test.cpp, handoff_controller tests}; qemu_plugin and vsim
  rebuild only (both consume the header).
- Acceptance: a marker binary runs to completion standalone on
  `--model fast` and `--model cycle`, and still hands off on hybrid.
- Deps: F1. State: todo

### F3: marker-sweep (behavioral)
Emit the new encodings everywhere markers are written; update the two
scanners outside the shared header; ship a user-facing marker header.
- enter_vsim/exit_vsim asm in tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h.
- asm fixtures embedding raw `csrwi 0x7C0` (handoff.S, handoff_exit.S,
  handoff_roundtrip.S, rt_*.S - grep `0x7C0|milmb`), incl. rt_pc_jump
  poison markers.

## Problem

1. The in-binary ROI markers are `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on
   the Andes core: the exit marker enables ILM at base 0 and kills any
   standalone run (`--model fast` trap loop). So today one binary cannot
   carry markers AND run on all engines.
2. Users want to pick the ROI like setting two breakpoints in an IDE:
   click a line, the IDE knows `file.c:42`, the tool does the rest. Today
   the only external anchors are symbol names or raw `0x` addresses.

## Design (one mechanism, three front-ends)

Both engines already reduce every trigger to a PC watch:
- vsim: `csr_trigger.hpp` pre-scans the code bytes for marker encodings
  and builds a pc->kind map; PC mode injects via `add_pc_hit()`.
- QEMU plugin: matches the marker encoding at translate time, or takes
  `enter_pc=0x...`.

So the engine layer stays untouched. ROI = a pair of PCs. What changes is
how the pair gets named:

| Front-end          | Source                                  | Status |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------|
| in-binary markers  | HINT NOP pair (was: csrwi 0x7C0)        | F2/F3  |
| symbol / 0xaddr    | `--pc-start S --pc-end E`               | exists |
| file:line (IDE)    | `--pc-start main.c:42` via DWARF        | F4     |

### Marker fix: RISC-V HINT pair

Integer-computational instructions with rd=x0 are architectural NOPs on
every conforming RISC-V core (spec "HINT" space). Candidate encodings:

- ENTER:   `slti x0, x0, IMM_ENTER`   (OP-IMM, rd=0, 12-bit payload)
- EXIT:    `slti x0, x0, IMM_EXIT`
- RUNTIME: `slt  x0, rs1, x0`         (R-type, rd=0; kind read from rs1
                                       at retire, same as today's
                                       `csrw 0x7C0, rs1`)

Properties: true NOP on fast, cycle, hybrid AND real silicon (MILMB
hazard gone, the docs' "never run marker binaries standalone" warning is
deleted); `slti`/`slt` have no compressed form, so the plugin `sz==4`
gate and the vsim 16/32 scanner invariant hold unchanged.

F2 must verify the exact imm values against the unpriv spec HINT table
and must not collide with allocated standard hints (Zihintntl uses
`add x0, x0, x2..x5`; Zihintpause uses a FENCE form) or Andes extensions.

`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` learn a third form, `path.c:NN`:

- first-hit semantics in loops (same as today's pc mode),

  the existing advice holds (anchor on calls / memory ops).

content.text:
The idea: keep one engine mechanism (ROI = a pair of PCs) and add new front-ends for naming that pair. No engine change is needed for the IDE story. Roadmap draft is in `roi_markers.md`; here is the design to discuss.

## Why this is the right shape

I checked the code first, and the key fact is: **both engines already reduce every trigger to a PC watch.**

- vsim never executes the CSR as a trigger. `csr_trigger.hpp` pre-scans the code bytes for the marker encoding and builds a `pc -> kind` map. PC mode just inserts into that same map (`add_pc_hit`).
- The QEMU plugin matches the marker encoding at translate time, or takes `enter_pc=0x...`.

So "marker" was never really "a CSR write the engine reacts to". It is "a recognizable byte pattern whose address becomes the trigger PC". That means we can swap the pattern, or skip the pattern entirely, without touching the handoff machinery.

## Part A - fix the marker pair (the CSR issue)

Replace `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` with a **RISC-V HINT pair**, e.g.:

```
ENTER:   slti x0, x0, IMM_A      EXIT: slti x0, x0, IMM_B
RUNTIME: slt  x0, rs1, x0        (dynamic kind in rs1, like csrw 0x7C0,rs1 today)
```

Any integer instruction with `rd=x0` is an architectural NOP on **every** conforming RISC-V core - fast model, cycle RTL, real silicon. The whole MILMB hazard disappears: one ELF with markers runs standalone everywhere. Bonus properties: `slti` has no compressed form, so the plugin's `sz==4` gate and vsim's 16/32-bit scanner stay valid; the change is literally one header (`insn_match.h`, shared by plugin and vsim) plus the asm in `enter_vsim()/exit_vsim()` and the raw bytes in `roi.sh`/asm fixtures.

Alternatives I rejected:

- **Another CSR**: the Andes vendor CSR space is a minefield; same class of bug waiting.
- **custom-0/1 opcodes** (gem5 m5-ops style): illegal instruction on cores that don't implement them - not portable, which is the whole point.
- **Marker functions in the runtime** (`roi_begin()` as a real `ret` function, driver finds the symbol): zero engine change, but adds ~2 insns of call overhead inside the measured window and dies on stripped binaries. HINTs are strictly better here since the matcher change is tiny anyway.

One verification task: pick imm values that don't collide with allocated standard hints (Zihintntl uses `add x0,x0,x2..x5`, Zihintpause uses a FENCE form) - and the real authority is just running it on the vsim RTL, which IS the Andes core.

## Part B - IDE "breakpoint" markers via file:line

Yes, the IDE giving a line number is exactly right, and it maps onto the existing pc trigger:

```
gutter click -> file.c:42
   -> driver resolves via DWARF line table -> 0x80000124 (matmul+0x18)
   -> existing plumbing: plugin enter_pc= / vsim --hybrid-exit-pc
   -> cycle figure back to the IDE
```

Concretely: `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` learn a third form, `main.c:42` (today: symbol or 0xaddr). Plus an `andes-sim resolve <elf> main.c:42 --json` subcommand so the IDE can validate a mark *before* a long run and show where it really landed.

The honest caveats - the same ones gdb breakpoints have:

- Needs `-g` (no codegen impact; we just add it to the documented two-flag command).
- At `-O2` a line can have no code or several copies. Policy: snap forward to the next line that has code, gdb-style, and **always print the resolution** so the user sees the drift. Silent snapping in a measurement tool would be lying about the window.
- Loops: first-hit semantics, same as pc mode today.

This makes the IDE contract editor-agnostic - it is just a CLI. The extension itself (gutter toggles, CodeLens showing "ROI: 14,668 cycles" at the start line) is a thin layer on top.

## What I want from you (PM)

1. **Rename `--trigger csr` to `--trigger marker`?** The old name is wrong even today. I propose a hard rename, no alias (pre-release).
2. **Which IDE first?** VS Code extension is cheapest. If your real target is AndeSight (Eclipse), F6 changes but F1-F5 are identical either way.
3. **DWARF resolution v1 = shell out to toolchain objdump** (`--dwarf=decodedline`)? The toolchain is already a doctor-checked dependency. A native `.debug_line` parser is possible later if runs must work without the toolchain installed.

Feature order in `roi_markers.md`: F1 rename (structural) -> F2 HINT encoding -> F3 sweep markers/fixtures/docs -> F4 file:line anchors -> F5 resolve subcommand -> F6 IDE layer.

# roi_markers.md - portable ROI markers + IDE line anchors

## Problem

1. The in-binary ROI markers are `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on
   the Andes core: the exit marker enables ILM at base 0 and kills any
   standalone run (`--model fast` trap loop). So today one binary cannot
   carry markers AND run on all engines.
2. Users want to pick the ROI like setting two breakpoints in an IDE:
   click a line, the IDE knows `file.c:42`, the tool does the rest. Today
   the only external anchors are symbol names or raw `0x` addresses.

## Design (one mechanism, three front-ends)

Both engines already reduce every trigger to a PC watch:
- vsim: `csr_trigger.hpp` pre-scans the code bytes for marker encodings
  and builds a pc->kind map; PC mode injects via `add_pc_hit()`.
- QEMU plugin: matches the marker encoding at translate time, or takes
  `enter_pc=0x...`.

So the engine layer stays untouched. ROI = a pair of PCs. What changes is
how the pair gets named:

| Front-end          | Source                                  | Status |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------|
| in-binary markers  | HINT NOP pair (was: csrwi 0x7C0)        | F2/F3  |
| symbol / 0xaddr    | `--pc-start S --pc-end E`               | exists |
| file:line (IDE)    | `--pc-start main.c:42` via DWARF        | F4     |

### Marker fix: RISC-V HINT pair

Integer-computational instructions with rd=x0 are architectural NOPs on
every conforming RISC-V core (spec "HINT" space). Candidate encodings:

- ENTER:   `slti x0, x0, IMM_ENTER`   (OP-IMM, rd=0, 12-bit payload)
- EXIT:    `slti x0, x0, IMM_EXIT`
- RUNTIME: `slt  x0, rs1, x0`         (R-type, rd=0; kind read from rs1
                                       at retire, same as today's
                                       `csrw 0x7C0, rs1`)

Properties: true NOP on fast, cycle, hybrid AND real silicon (MILMB
hazard gone, the docs' "never run marker binaries standalone" warning is
deleted); `slti`/`slt` have no compressed form, so the plugin `sz==4`
gate and the vsim 16/32 scanner invariant hold unchanged.

F2 must verify the exact imm values against the unpriv spec HINT table
and must not collide with allocated standard hints (Zihintntl uses
`add x0, x0, x2..x5`; Zihintpause uses a FENCE form) or Andes extensions.

### IDE anchors: file:line -> PC

`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` learn a third form, `path.c:NN`:
- Resolve via the DWARF line table (v1: shell out to toolchain
  `objdump --dwarf=decodedline`; toolchain is already a doctor-checked
  dependency). Pick the lowest `is_stmt` address for the exact line.
- If the line has no code (optimized out), snap forward to the next line
  that has code, gdb-style, and PRINT the snap.
- Always echo the resolution: `main.c:42 -> 0x80000124 (matmul+0x18)`.
- Requires `-g` in the user's compile flags (no codegen impact; add to
  the documented two-flag command).

Known limits (same as any debugger breakpoint, document them):
- first-hit semantics in loops (same as today's pc mode),
- at -O2 a line can map to several PCs or move; for tight attribution
  the existing advice holds (anchor on calls / memory ops).

IDE contract is then trivial and editor-agnostic: gutter click ->
`file:line` -> `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc
--pc-start A.c:10 --pc-end A.c:20 app.elf` -> cycle figure back.

## Features

### F1: trigger-rename (structural)
Rename the user surface `--trigger csr` -> `--trigger marker` (the name
is wrong even today: vsim never executes it as a CSR, it PC-watches).
No alias kept (pre-release). e2e `MODE=csr` -> `MODE=marker`.
- Key files: driver/{cli.cpp, main.cpp, cmd_run.cpp, hybrid.cpp,
  run_plan.cpp, engine_registry.cpp, models.hpp, *_test.cpp}, hsim.py
  (lockstep, parity), tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh,
  tests/andes_sim/*, tests/hsim/*, docs/USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md.
- Deps: none. Pure rename commit (Tidy First), behavior unchanged.
- State: todo

### F2: hint-encoding (behavioral)
Rewrite `hybrid_match_handoff_insn` for the HINT encodings (remove the
CSR form entirely). Update the inverse encoders + doctest first (RED).
- Key files: include/hybrid/insn_match.h,
  verilator/tests/hybrid/{insn_match.test.cpp, insn_encoders.hpp,
  csr_trigger.test.cpp, handoff_controller tests}; qemu_plugin and vsim
  rebuild only (both consume the header).
- Acceptance: a marker binary runs to completion standalone on
  `--model fast` and `--model cycle`, and still hands off on hybrid.
- Deps: F1. State: todo

### F3: marker-sweep (behavioral)
Emit the new encodings everywhere markers are written; update the two
scanners outside the shared header; ship a user-facing marker header.
- enter_vsim/exit_vsim asm in tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h.
- asm fixtures embedding raw `csrwi 0x7C0` (handoff.S, handoff_exit.S,
  handoff_roundtrip.S, rt_*.S - grep `0x7C0|milmb`), incl. rt_pc_jump
  poison markers.
- tests/lib/roi.sh awk encodings (7c005073/7c00d073 -> new bytes).
- NEW runtime/roi.h: `andes_sim_roi_begin()/end()` inline HINTs,
  installed to build/runtime by runtime/Makefile; now safe in vplat
  binaries (markers + standalone compose).
- Delete the MILMB warnings from docs/USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md,
  tests/fixtures comments.
- Deps: F2. State: todo

### F4: line-anchors (behavioral)
`--pc-start/--pc-end` accept `file.c:NN`; DWARF resolution with
snap-and-report as above. Implement in BOTH drivers (hsim.py lockstep,
~40 lines of python) so help text and parity stay meaningful.
- Key files: driver/line_anchor.{cpp,hpp} (new, beside elf_syms),
  driver/cli.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, hsim.py,
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_line_anchor.sh, docs/USER_GUIDE.md
  (add `-g` to the two-flag command).
- Deps: none (rides the existing pc trigger; F1 only renames). State: todo

### F5: resolve-subcommand
`andes-sim resolve <elf> <anchor>` prints pc, symbol+offset, file:line
for any anchor form (symbol, 0xaddr, file:line); `--json` for IDEs.
Lets an IDE validate a gutter mark before a long run, and shows users
where a snapped anchor really landed. Lockstep in hsim.py.
- Key files: driver/cmd_resolve.cpp (new), main.cpp, hsim.py,
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_resolve.sh.
- Deps: F4. State: todo

### F6: ide-integration
v0: docs recipe (VS Code tasks.json with prompt inputs feeding
file:line). v1: thin extension (tools/vscode-andes-sim/): two gutter
toggles "ROI start/end" like breakpoints, a "Measure ROI" command that
runs F5 resolve + the hybrid run, CodeLens shows the cycle figure at
the start line.
- Deps: F4, F5. State: todo (blocked on IDE choice, see below)

## Open questions for PM

1. Hard-rename `--trigger csr` -> `--trigger marker`, no alias - OK?
2. Which IDE first? VS Code extension is the cheapest; if the target is
   AndeSight (Eclipse), F6 becomes an Eclipse plugin but F1-F5 are
   identical either way (the CLI contract is editor-agnostic).
3. F4 v1 shells out to toolchain objdump for DWARF (native .debug_line
   parser later if a toolchain-free run matters) - acceptable?

message.content: what does RUNTIME = slt x0, rs1, x0  mean?

content.text:
It is the "decide at run time" marker: a NOP that names a register, and the *value in that register* at retire decides whether the ROI ends.

Today's CSR version is `csrw 0x7C0, rs1` (`HYBRID_HANDOFF_RUNTIME` in `insn_match.h`). Unlike `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`, where "this is the exit" is baked into the instruction bits, here vsim's handoff controller decodes which register `rs1` is, reads that GPR when the instruction retires, and fires the drain only if it holds 1 (`handoff_controller.hpp:72`: `fire = (read_gpr(rs1) == 1u)`). So one marker site in a loop can mean "not yet" on most iterations (register holds 0) and "exit now" on the last one (register holds 1), with no separate exit branch:

```asm
loop:
  ...
  sltiu t0, t1, 1      # t0 = 1 on the final iteration
  csrw  0x7C0, t0      # today: fires drain only when t0 == 1
  bnez  t1, loop
```

The replacement `slt x0, rs1, x0` keeps exactly this contract with a safe encoding:

- `slt` writes "rs1 < rs2" into rd. With `rd = x0` the result is thrown away, so it is an architectural NOP on every core (HINT space) - that fixes the MILMB problem for this marker too.
- `rd` and `rs2` are pinned to x0; the `rs1` field is the only free slot, and it carries the register name, same as the CSR form did. The matcher becomes `(insn & 0xFFF07FFF) == 0x00002033`, and the controller extracts rs1 from the same bit positions it already reads (bits 19:15).

So nothing changes in behavior or in the controller's fire logic - only the byte pattern the scanner looks for. The instruction is just a tagged NOP; the register content is the actual message.

Found the honest answer: **nothing uses it.** No fixture, no test script, no driver path emits the runtime-valued marker - the only references are its own unit tests (`insn_match.test.cpp`, `csr_trigger.test.cpp`, `handoff_controller.test.cpp`, `handoff_site.test.cpp`). The QEMU plugin even ignores the kind (it only acts on ENTER).

What it was *designed* for: cases where the exit decision is computed while running, not fixed at a code location. Two intended patterns:

1. **One marker inside a loop.** "Exit the ROI after iteration N": the loop writes 0 to a register on normal iterations and 1 on the last one, and the single marker site fires only when the register holds 1. With the static `csrwi` form you would instead need a branch to a separate exit-marker site.
2. **A marker behind a variable.** `csrwi` needs a compile-time constant immediate. If a helper like `roi_mark(flag)` takes `flag` as a function argument, the compiler must use the register form `csrw 0x7C0, reg` - the value isn't known until run time.

Both are hypothetical here - no workload in the repo ever needed them.

**Recommendation: drop RUNTIME in F2 instead of porting it.** That deletes the `funct3==001` arm from the matcher, the `RUNTIME` case plus `decode_csrrw_rs1` GPR-read from `handoff_controller.hpp`, and the related unit tests - the matcher becomes two exact 32-bit compares, nothing more. If a conditional-exit need ever shows up, we re-add it then with a HINT encoding (`slt x0, rs1, x0` is reserved and waiting). Carrying an unused arm through the rewrite is exactly the dead weight your rewrite-don't-patch rule is meant to kill.

If you agree, I'll mark RUNTIME as "dropped (unused)" in `roi_markers.md` and the F2 table shrinks to ENTER/EXIT only.

# roi_markers.md - portable ROI markers (Part A) + trigger rename

DECIDED (2026-06-11): Part A + rename `csr` -> `marker`. Scope = F1-F3.
Part B (file:line / IDE anchors) is DEFERRED - kept at the bottom for later.

## Problem

The in-binary ROI markers are `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on
the Andes core: the exit marker enables ILM at base 0 and kills any
standalone run (`--model fast` trap loop). So today one binary cannot
carry markers AND run on all engines. Also the trigger name `csr` is
wrong: vsim never executes the CSR; it pre-scans code bytes for the
encoding and PC-watches (`csr_trigger.hpp`), and the QEMU plugin matches
the encoding at translate time. A marker is "a recognizable byte pattern
whose address becomes the trigger PC" - so swap the pattern for one that
is a NOP everywhere.

## Design: RISC-V HINT pair

Integer-computational instructions with rd=x0 are architectural NOPs on
every conforming RISC-V core (spec HINT space). New encodings:

| Kind    | Asm                     | Encoding match                       |
|---------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| ENTER   | `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`    | insn == 0x5A002013                   |
| EXIT    | `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`    | insn == 0x5A102013                   |
| RUNTIME | `slt  x0, rs1, x0`      | (insn & 0xFFF07FFF) == 0x00002033; kind read from rs1 at retire (replaces `csrw 0x7C0, rs1`) |

Properties:
- True NOP on fast, cycle, hybrid AND real silicon. MILMB hazard gone;
  one marker ELF runs standalone everywhere. All MILMB warnings in docs
  get deleted.
- `slti`/`slt` have no compressed form: the plugin `sz==4` gate and the
  vsim 16/32-bit scanner invariant hold unchanged.
- No collision with allocated standard hints: Zihintntl is
  `add x0, x0, x2..x5` (funct3=000, we use 010), Zihintpause is a FENCE
  form. F2 verifies the imm choice against the unpriv spec HINT table
  and confirms NOP behavior on the vsim RTL (the real authority).

Rejected alternatives: another vendor CSR (same bug class), custom-0/1
opcodes (illegal insn on cores without them), runtime marker functions
(call overhead inside the window, dies on stripped binaries).

## Features

### F1: trigger-rename (structural)
One name everywhere: the trigger/mode value `csr` -> `marker`. Hard
rename, no alias (pre-release). The CSR-instruction references
(`csrwi 0x7C0`, insn_match.h, fixtures) are NOT touched here - they die
in F2/F3. Internal vsim names (csr_trigger.hpp, CsrTrigger) stay; they
are submodule-internal and can be tidied later.
- C++ driver: hybrid.cpp (default kind, dispatch, kanata gate, error
  string), engine_registry.cpp (triggers list), models.hpp (notes),
  main.cpp + cmd_run.cpp (help/comments), run_plan.cpp (kind compare),
  driver tests (cli_test, hybrid_test, plan_itest, run_test, json_test).
- Harness: tests/e2e.sh (`TRIGGER_MODE` default + error msg),
  scripts/run_e2e.sh (MODE=both expansion, log names).
- Golden (lockstep, same harness): hsim.py mode key "csr" -> "marker"
  (MODE_KEYS table, --mode choices, `test --mode` choices, how_to_run
  strings); tests/hsim/*.sh that pass --mode csr.
- Tests: tests/andes_sim/*.sh using --trigger csr;
  tests/hybrid/e2e_warmup_csr.sh (rename file + content).
- Docs: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md, CLAUDE.md,
  docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb.
- TDD: update the surface tests first (RED), rename (GREEN). Commit as
  structural; behavior identical.
- State: todo

### F2: hint-encoding (behavioral)
Rewrite `hybrid_match_handoff_insn` for the table above (delete the CSR
form entirely; rewrite, don't patch). Update the inverse encoders and
doctest first (RED).
- Key files: include/hybrid/state ABI sibling insn_match.h;
  verilator/tests/hybrid/{insn_match.test.cpp, insn_encoders.hpp,
  csr_trigger.test.cpp, handoff_controller/handoff_site tests}
  (submodule commit + pointer bump); qemu_plugin and vsim consume the
  header - rebuild only.
- Host-side doctest run first (no container needed), then vsim rebuild.
- State: todo

### F3: marker-sweep (behavioral)
Emit the new encodings everywhere markers are written; update scanners
outside the shared header; ship the user-facing marker header.
- enter_vsim/exit_vsim asm: tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h.
- asm fixtures embedding raw csrwi/encodings: handoff.S, handoff_exit.S,
  handoff_roundtrip.S, rt_*.S (grep `0x7C0|7c005073|7c00d073|milmb`),
  incl. rt_pc_jump poison markers; test_gemm_* generators;
  rt_c_no_trigger_exit.c comment.
- tests/lib/roi.sh awk raw-byte match: 7c005073/7c00d073 -> 5a002013/
  5a102013 (keep first-ENTER / LAST-EXIT selection logic).
- NEW runtime/roi.h: `andes_sim_roi_begin()/end()` inline HINT asm with
  "memory" clobber (same cycle-attribution contract as rt_c_helpers.h),
  installed to build/runtime by runtime/Makefile; markers are now safe
  in vplat binaries (markers + standalone compose).
- Delete MILMB warnings: docs/USER_GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md, fixture comments.
- Acceptance: full e2e green (MODE=both); a marker fixture runs to
  completion standalone on `--model fast` AND `--model cycle` (new
  smoke test), and still hands off on hybrid.
- State: todo

COMMIT NOTE: F2 and F3 land as ONE behavioral commit. The encoding swap
breaks every existing fixture until the sweep lands; splitting them
would leave a commit with a red e2e suite.

## Deferred: Part B - file:line / IDE anchors (not scheduled)

`--pc-start/--pc-end` learn `file.c:NN` resolved via the DWARF line
table (snap-and-report, gdb-style, needs -g); `andes-sim resolve`
subcommand (--json) for IDE pre-validation; thin IDE layer (gutter
ROI toggles -> run -> cycle figure as CodeLens). Editor-agnostic CLI
contract; open question when scheduled: VS Code vs AndeSight first.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andes-sim driver: driver/ -> build/andes-sim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andes-sim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andes-sim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F3 contract: the whole link recipe collapses into two flags --
#
#   gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
#       -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c -o hello.elf
#
# The specs file swaps the startfile to our crt0.o, appends -T andes-sim.ld
# and rewrites the library sequence to
# `--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc --end-group` (no -lgloss,
# no semihosting). The produced ELF must run on all three engines.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/hello.c" <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello from specs\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl vplat_roi_end\nvplat_roi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# The two-flag user command (plus a link map for the no-gloss assert).
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andes-sim.specs "$TMP/hello.c" -o "$TMP/hello.elf" \
  -Wl,-Map,"$TMP/hello.map" || fail "two-flag specs link failed"

grep 'libandes_sim_runtime\.a' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null \
  || fail "link map does not pull libandes_sim_runtime.a"
if grep 'gloss' "$TMP/hello.map" >/dev/null; then
  fail "link map pulls a libgloss (semihosting leaked into the link)"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI-marker portability contract (roi_markers.md F3): the markers shipped
# in <andes_sim/roi.h> are RISC-V HINTs (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1), i.e.
# architectural NOPs. ONE marker binary must therefore
#
#   1. run to completion standalone on --model fast  (the old csrwi 0x7C0
#      markers died here: 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores, the exit marker
#      enabled ILM at base 0 and trapped forever),
#   2. run to completion standalone on the cycle engine,
#   3. hand off on --model hybrid --trigger marker and print window_cycles.
#
# The same two-flag user command as F8; the header rides the -B prefix
# (gcc adds <prefix>/include to the include path).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"
[ -f "$RT/include/andes_sim/roi.h" ] || fail "runtime did not install andes_sim/roi.h"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/roi.c" <<'EOF'
#include <andes_sim/roi.h>
#include <stdio.h>

static volatile unsigned src[64], dst[64];

int main(void)
{
  printf("before roi\n");
  andes_sim_roi_begin();
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++)  /* memory-anchored kernel */
    dst[i] = src[i] + i;
  andes_sim_roi_end();
  printf("after roi\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andes-sim.specs "$TMP/roi.c" -o "$TMP/roi.elf" \
  || fail "two-flag build with <andes_sim/roi.h> failed"

# The binary must embed exactly the published wire encodings.
OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
DIS=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/roi.elf")
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a002013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "enter marker 0x5A002013 not found in disassembly"
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a102013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "exit marker 0x5A102013 not found in disassembly"

# 1. fast, standalone: markers are NOPs, program must finish.
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --model fast "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "fast: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "fast: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 2. cycle, standalone: same.
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "cycle: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "cycle: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 3. hybrid, marker trigger: the same markers drive the handoff.
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --model hybrid --trigger marker \
        --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[marker window_cycles\] [0-9]+' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing window_cycles line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "markers are HINT NOPs: one ELF runs standalone on fast+cycle and hands off on hybrid"

/* andes_sim/roi.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andes_sim_roi_begin()/andes_sim_roi_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--model hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --model fast, --model cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ROI_H
#define ANDES_SIM_ROI_H

static inline void andes_sim_roi_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andes_sim_roi_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDES_SIM_ROI_H */

# Build the user-facing andes-sim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandes_sim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andes-sim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andes-sim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landes_sim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ar

OUT ?= ../build/runtime

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V
# arch attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andes-sim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andes-sim.specs

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandes_sim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andes-sim.ld: andes-sim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andes-sim.specs: andes-sim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: built THROUGH the shipped runtime library with the same two-flag
# command users type (-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs), so the
# suites regression-test the real artifact. No libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs.
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandes_sim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andes-sim.specs
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(HELPERS_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andes-sim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andes-sim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T $(LDSCRIPT) \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT_DIR).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andes-sim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all four artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andes-sim.specs
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(LDSCRIPT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * CSR mode pattern-matches the csrwi insns directly; the helpers do not
 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
}

/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their csrwi, so the markers anchor
 * a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS, no csrwi)
 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
static inline void roi_anchor(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED-then-green test for gemm_modes.md F1: make tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c
# serve BOTH the marked and the markerless build from one source.
#
# Pins three source properties the rest of the GEMM-unification depends on:
#   1. noinline kernel  - `vmatmul_kernel` survives -O1 as a real symbol, so
#      icount-mode PC-range assertions can anchor on it.
#   2. marker macro     - compiling with -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS drops the
#      csrwi 0x7C0 enter/exit markers (needed by the count-driven modes;
#      otherwise the CSR matcher would drain AT the marker first).
#   3. behavior-identity - the default (marked) build still emits both markers.
#
# Self-contained: resolves the Andes toolchain via tests/lib/paths.sh (config.env)
# and builds through the fixtures Makefile. Skips (77) if the toolchain is absent.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] || [ ! -x "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" ]; then
  echo "SKIP test_gemm_source: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set/usable"
  exit 77
fi
CC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"

cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
SRC=rt_c_v_matmul.c
ELF=rt_c_v_matmul.elf
[ -f "$SRC" ] || fail "missing source $SRC"

# --- 1. marked build: noinline kernel symbol present -----------------------
# NB: feed grep via here-strings, not `cmd | grep -q`. Under `set -o pipefail`
# grep -q exits on first match and SIGPIPEs the producer (141), which pipefail
# then propagates as a spurious failure on large inputs (e.g. the objdump).
make -s TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "make $ELF failed"
syms=$("$NM" "$ELF")
grep -qw vmatmul_kernel <<<"$syms" \
  || fail "noinline broken: 'vmatmul_kernel' is not a symbol in $ELF (still inlined)"
ok "marked build keeps vmatmul_kernel as a linkable symbol (noinline)"

# --- 2. behavior-identity: marked build still emits both csrwi markers ------
# Match the instruction OPCODE (toolchain-independent): the Andes objdump
# prints CSR 0x7C0 by its vendor name (milmb), so a textual "0x7c0" match
# misses. 7c005073 = slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 (enter); 7c00d073 = slti x0, x0, 0x5A1 (exit) --
# the exact encodings insn_match.h drains on.
dump=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF")
grep -qw 7c005073 <<<"$dump" \
  || fail "marked build lost the enter marker (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0 / opcode 7c005073)"
grep -qw 7c00d073 <<<"$dump" \
  || fail "marked build lost the exit marker (slti x0, x0, 0x5A1 / opcode 7c00d073)"
ok "marked build still emits both enter/exit csrwi 0x7C0 markers (opcodes)"

# --- 3. markerless macro drops the markers, keeps the kernel ----------------
# Compile-only (-S) with the same -march as RT_C_V_CFLAGS; no link/libs needed
# to observe whether the csrwi markers are emitted.
ASM=$(mktemp -t gemm-free-XXXXXX.s)
trap 'rm -f "$ASM"' EXIT
"$CC" -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Iruntime -Wall \
  -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -S "$SRC" -o "$ASM" \
  || fail "markerless compile (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS) failed"
if grep -qE 'csrwi\s+0x7c0|csrwi.*0x7C0' "$ASM"; then
  fail "markerless build still emits csrwi 0x7c0 markers (HYBRID_MARKERLESS guard missing)"
fi
ok "markerless build (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS) emits no csrwi 0x7c0 markers"
grep -qE '^vmatmul_kernel:|vmatmul_kernel, ?@function' "$ASM" \
  || fail "markerless build dropped the vmatmul_kernel function"
ok "markerless build still contains vmatmul_kernel"

echo "PASS test_gemm_source"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED-then-green test for gemm_modes.md F2: the markerless GEMM twin ELF.
#
# F1 made rt_c_v_matmul.c serve both builds; F2 adds the Makefile rule that
# emits `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` (same source, compiled -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS).
# Asserts the built twin:
#   1. builds via the fixtures Makefile,
#   2. keeps vmatmul_kernel as a symbol (icount mode anchors on it),
#   3. carries NO csrwi 0x7C0 markers (so the count-driven plugin modes are
#      not drained at a marker before reaching their count target).
#
# Reachability (icount target landing inside the kernel) is asserted by the
# end-to-end icount round-trip, not here -- this test needs no QEMU,
# only the toolchain.

[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac

# --- roi_markers_from_disasm: derive pc-mode boundaries from milmb markers ---
# Lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no per-fixture config: ENTER is the
# entry marker `csrwi milmb,0` (enc 7c005073), EXIT is the LAST exit marker
# `csrwi milmb,1` (enc 7c00d073). Both are the marker PCs themselves -- the
# plugin/vsim resume one insn past the trigger (compute_handoff_pc=vaddr+size),
# reproducing CSR mode's switch points. Inputs are `objdump -d` fragments.

# 8. in-order fixture: entry marker -> single exit marker.
DISASM_INORDER='  10023c: 7c005073  csrwi milmb,0
  100240: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100244: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_INORDER") \
  || fail "in-order: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "10023c 100240" ] || fail "in-order: want '10023c 100240' got '$got'"

# 9. jump-over-poison fixture (rt_pc_jump): the c.j skips dead exit markers;
#    the LAST 7c00d073 is the real, reachable exit -- not the first.
DISASM_JUMP='  100000: 7c005073  csrwi milmb,0
  100004: a83d  c.j 0x100042
  100006: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  10000a: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100042: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100046: 4601  c.li a2,0'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_JUMP") \
  || fail "jump: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "100000 100042" ] || fail "jump: want '100000 100042' (last exit) got '$got'"

# 10. no markers -> nonzero return, empty output.
DISASM_NONE='  100000: 1141  c.addi sp,sp,-16
  100002: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_NONE"); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-markers: expected nonzero return, got rc=0"
[ -z "$got" ]   || fail "no-markers: expected empty output, got '$got'"

echo "[roi_resolve] PASS"

50	#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the milmb ROI markers a fixture
51	#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
52	#     ENTER = the entry marker     `csrwi milmb,0`  (encoding 7c005073)
53	#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker  `csrwi milmb,1`  (encoding 7c00d073)
54	#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
55	#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
56	#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
57	#   CSR mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT keeps
58	#   the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison `csrwi milmb,1`
59	#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
60	#   dead one. The encodings are unambiguous (csr 0x7c0, uimm 0/1), so the
61	#   raw-bytes match needs no CSR-name table from objdump.
62	#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
63	#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
64	#   per-fixture config; ./andes-sim run still passes explicit boundaries.
65	roi_markers_from_disasm() {
66	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
67	    $2 == "7c005073" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
68	    $2 == "7c00d073"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
69	    END {
70	      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
71	      else                              { exit 1 }
72	    }
73	  '
74	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the milmb ROI markers a fixture
#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
#     ENTER = the entry marker     `csrwi milmb,0`  (encoding 7c005073)
#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker  `csrwi milmb,1`  (encoding 7c00d073)
#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
#   CSR mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT keeps
#   the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison `csrwi milmb,1`
#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
#   dead one. The encodings are unambiguous (csr 0x7c0, uimm 0/1), so the
#   raw-bytes match needs no CSR-name table from objdump.
#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
#   per-fixture config; ./andes-sim run still passes explicit boundaries.
roi_markers_from_disasm() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
    $2 == "7c005073" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
    $2 == "7c00d073"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
    END {
      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
      else                              { exit 1 }
    }
  '
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"

fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }

# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
0000000000100000 T main'

# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"

# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"

# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output.
got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"

# 4. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"

# --- roi_resolve_pair: env-required + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---

# 5. unset ROI_START/ROI_END -> error (no implicit fallback).
unset ROI_START ROI_END
out=$(roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t 2>&1)
[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "unset pair: expected nonzero return"
case "$out" in *"ROI_START and ROI_END"*) ;; *) fail "unset pair: missing required-vars message: '$out'";; esac

# 6. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex resolve to ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC.
ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"

# 7. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac

# --- roi_markers_from_disasm: derive pc-mode boundaries from milmb markers ---
# Lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no per-fixture config: ENTER is the
# entry marker `csrwi milmb,0` (enc 7c005073), EXIT is the LAST exit marker

# reproducing CSR mode's switch points. Inputs are `objdump -d` fragments.

# 8. in-order fixture: entry marker -> single exit marker.
DISASM_INORDER='  10023c: 7c005073  csrwi milmb,0
  100240: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100244: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_INORDER") \
  || fail "in-order: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "10023c 100240" ] || fail "in-order: want '10023c 100240' got '$got'"

# 9. jump-over-poison fixture (rt_pc_jump): the c.j skips dead exit markers;
#    the LAST 7c00d073 is the real, reachable exit -- not the first.
DISASM_JUMP='  100000: 7c005073  csrwi milmb,0
  100004: a83d  c.j 0x100042
  100006: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  10000a: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100042: 7c00d073  csrwi milmb,1
  100046: 4601  c.li a2,0'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_JUMP") \
  || fail "jump: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "100000 100042" ] || fail "jump: want '100000 100042' (last exit) got '$got'"

# 10. no markers -> nonzero return, empty output.

  100002: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_NONE"); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-markers: expected nonzero return, got rc=0"
[ -z "$got" ]   || fail "no-markers: expected empty output, got '$got'"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F14: `./hsim.py estimate <elf>` always runs the workload to
# its natural exit (semihosting EXIT), drains state in the plugin's
# atexit callback, and uses the plugin-counted retired-insn count as
# N_total in the SimPoint aggregation formula. Run-to-exit is the only
# behavior -- there is no --icount knob to cap the profile.
#
# Workload: tests/fixtures/rt_c_no_trigger_exit.elf. ~50K-100K insns total,
# no csrwi 0x7C0, exits via libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT.
#
# Pipeline (profile + cluster + per-phase drains) caps at 120s for headroom.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_no_trigger_exit.elf"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (run ./hsim.py build first)"

cd "$ROOT"

# 1. Fixture sanity: must contain zero csrwi 0x7C0,* insns.
# Locate the riscv64 objdump (mirrors fixtures/Makefile TOOLCHAIN lookup).
OBJDUMP=""
if [ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" ]; then
  OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
elif command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OBJDUMP=$(command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump)
fi
if [ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]; then
  count=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE 'csrwi[[:space:]]+0x7[Cc]0' || true)
  [ "${count:-0}" -eq 0 ] \
    || fail "fixture $ELF has $count csrwi 0x7C0 insn(s); F14 needs zero"
  ok "fixture has zero csrwi 0x7C0 insns"
else
  echo "[skip] objdump not found; skipping csrwi check"
fi

# 2. estimate --help describes the natural-program-exit profile pass and
#    no longer advertises a --icount flag.
out=$("$HSIM" estimate --help 2>&1) || fail "estimate --help non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -qiE 'natural program exit|exit.*plugin atexit|run to (program )?exit' \
  || fail "estimate --help missing 'natural program exit' hint:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qE -- '--icount' \
  && fail "estimate --help still mentions removed --icount:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate --help documents run-to-exit profile (no --icount)"

# 3. Real estimate run uses run-to-exit path (no --icount knob to pass).
set +e
out=$(timeout 120 "$HSIM" estimate "$ELF" --slice 1000 --max-k 2 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "estimate (no --icount) rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate run exits 0 (no --icount, always run-to-exit)"

# 4. Output has estimated_cycles=<int>, > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'estimated_cycles=<int>' line:"$'\n'"$out"
EST=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${EST:-0}" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "estimated_cycles must be > 0, got '$EST':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimated_cycles=$EST"

# 5. N_total surfaced in the report line must be > 0 and >> 2000
# (loop iters lower bound; libgloss startup adds more).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'N=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'N=<int>' in summary line:"$'\n'"$out"
NTOT=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'N=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${NTOT:-0}" -gt 2000 ] \
  || fail "N_total must reflect real insn count (>2000), got '$NTOT':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "N_total=$NTOT (from plugin atexit minstret counter)"

# 6. Per-phase rows show delta_mcycle > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing per-phase 'delta_mcycle=<int>' rows:"$'\n'"$out"
N_PHASES=$(echo "$out" | grep -cE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+')
[ "$N_PHASES" -ge 1 ] \
  || fail "need at least 1 per-phase row, got $N_PHASES:"$'\n'"$out"
while IFS= read -r delta; do
  [ "$delta" -gt 0 ] \
    || fail "delta_mcycle must be > 0, got '$delta':"$'\n'"$out"
done < <(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' | cut -d= -f2)
ok "$N_PHASES per-phase row(s) with delta_mcycle > 0"

# 7. weighted_CPI is sensible (positive, < 100).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'weighted_CPI=<float>' in summary:"$'\n'"$out"
CPI=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
awk -v c="$CPI" 'BEGIN { exit (c > 0 && c < 100) ? 0 : 1 }' \
  || fail "weighted_CPI=$CPI out of plausible range:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "weighted_CPI=$CPI in plausible range"

echo "PASS test_hsim_estimate_drain_at_exit"

#    (5a002013 = slti x0,x0,0x5A0 enter / 5a102013 = exit).
# Locate the riscv64 objdump (mirrors fixtures/Makefile TOOLCHAIN lookup).
OBJDUMP=""
if [ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" ]; then

elif command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  OBJDUMP=$(command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump)
fi
if [ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]; then
  count=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE 'csrwi[[:space:]]+0x7[Cc]0' || true)
  [ "${count:-0}" -eq 0 ] \
    || fail "fixture $ELF has $count csrwi 0x7C0 insn(s); F14 needs zero"
  ok "fixture has zero csrwi 0x7C0 insns"
else
  echo "[skip] objdump not found; skipping csrwi check"
fi

# 2. estimate --help describes the natural-program-exit profile pass and
#    no longer advertises a --icount flag.
out=$("$HSIM" estimate --help 2>&1) || fail "estimate --help non-zero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -qiE 'natural program exit|exit.*plugin atexit|run to (program )?exit' \
  || fail "estimate --help missing 'natural program exit' hint:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qE -- '--icount' \
  && fail "estimate --help still mentions removed --icount:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate --help documents run-to-exit profile (no --icount)"

# 3. Real estimate run uses run-to-exit path (no --icount knob to pass).
set +e
out=$(timeout 120 "$HSIM" estimate "$ELF" --slice 1000 --max-k 2 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "estimate (no --icount) rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimate run exits 0 (no --icount, always run-to-exit)"

# 4. Output has estimated_cycles=<int>, > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'estimated_cycles=<int>' line:"$'\n'"$out"
EST=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'estimated_cycles=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${EST:-0}" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "estimated_cycles must be > 0, got '$EST':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "estimated_cycles=$EST"

# 5. N_total surfaced in the report line must be > 0 and >> 2000
# (loop iters lower bound; libgloss startup adds more).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'N=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'N=<int>' in summary line:"$'\n'"$out"
NTOT=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'N=[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
[ "${NTOT:-0}" -gt 2000 ] \
  || fail "N_total must reflect real insn count (>2000), got '$NTOT':"$'\n'"$out"
ok "N_total=$NTOT (from plugin atexit minstret counter)"

# 6. Per-phase rows show delta_mcycle > 0.
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing per-phase 'delta_mcycle=<int>' rows:"$'\n'"$out"
N_PHASES=$(echo "$out" | grep -cE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+')
[ "$N_PHASES" -ge 1 ] \
  || fail "need at least 1 per-phase row, got $N_PHASES:"$'\n'"$out"
while IFS= read -r delta; do
  [ "$delta" -gt 0 ] \
    || fail "delta_mcycle must be > 0, got '$delta':"$'\n'"$out"
done < <(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'delta_mcycle=[0-9]+' | cut -d= -f2)
ok "$N_PHASES per-phase row(s) with delta_mcycle > 0"

# 7. weighted_CPI is sensible (positive, < 100).
echo "$out" | grep -qE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'weighted_CPI=<float>' in summary:"$'\n'"$out"
CPI=$(echo "$out" | grep -oE 'weighted_CPI=[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
awk -v c="$CPI" 'BEGIN { exit (c > 0 && c < 100) ? 0 : 1 }' \
  || fail "weighted_CPI=$CPI out of plausible range:"$'\n'"$out"
ok "weighted_CPI=$CPI in plausible range"

echo "PASS test_hsim_estimate_drain_at_exit"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED test for F3: `./hsim.py run <elf> --mode marker|pc --kanata FILE`.
#
# Produces a kanata pipeline log restricted to the ROI region of the
# hybrid run. marker-mode auto-derives ROI bounds from the resume PC and
# the unique exit-marker PC. pc-mode honors --pc-start/--pc-end.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim.py"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"

# Same convention as tests/lib/paths.sh: fall back to ./config.env when
# the toolchain isn't already on the env, so --objdump probing works
# without requiring `source ./setup.sh` first.
if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$ROOT/config.env"
fi

cd "$ROOT"

TMPDIR_ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t hsim-kanata-XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMPDIR_ROOT"' EXIT

# 1. --help advertises --kanata and --objdump on the run subcommand.
out=$("$HSIM" run --help 2>&1) || fail "run --help exit nonzero: $out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--kanata"  || fail "run --help missing --kanata:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--objdump" || fail "run --help missing --objdump:\n$out"
ok "run --help lists --kanata and --objdump"

# 2. --kanata with --mode icount -> rc=2 (the kanata-roi path only supports
#    marker/pc).
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount \
       --kanata "$TMPDIR_ROOT/x.kanata" 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--kanata with icount should rc=2, got $rc:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "kanata" || fail "icount rejection should mention kanata:\n$out"
ok "--kanata + --mode icount rejected (rc=2)"

# 3. marker-mode smoke: kanata file is created, non-empty, has Kanata header.
KFILE="$TMPDIR_ROOT/marker.kanata"
SMOKE_TIMEOUT=60
set +e
out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
        --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE" 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
[ -s "$KFILE" ] || fail "marker-mode: kanata file not created or empty: $KFILE"
head -1 "$KFILE" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file missing 'Kanata' header (first line):\n$(head -2 "$KFILE")"
# ROI window must have at least one fetched insn (I record) and one
# retired insn (R record). Both should appear after the LoopGate opens.
grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE" \
  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file has no I (start_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
grep -q "^R	" "$KFILE" \
  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file has no R (retire_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"
ok "marker-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"

# 4. marker-mode with --objdump: a load-line shows the disassembly. This
#    proves the OBJDUMP_FILE env reached vsim via e2e.sh.
DUMP="$TMPDIR_ROOT/rt_c_hello.S"
OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP_TOOL:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
if ! command -v "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[skip] objdump not found ($OBJDUMP_TOOL); skipping --objdump check"
else
  "$OBJDUMP_TOOL" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf > "$DUMP" \
    || fail "objdump -d failed for rt_c_hello.elf"
  KFILE2="$TMPDIR_ROOT/marker-dump.kanata"
  set +e
  out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
          --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE2" --objdump "$DUMP" 2>&1); rc=$?
  set -e
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker+objdump run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
  # With objdump, L records should embed the asm text after the PC.
  # Example: "L\t1\t0\t0x800000ec: csrwi  0x7c0,1"
  grep -E "^L\b.*0x[0-9a-f]+: [a-z]" "$KFILE2" >/dev/null \
    || fail "marker+objdump: no L record with disassembly text:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE2")"
  ok "marker-mode --kanata --objdump embeds disassembly"
fi

# 5. pc-mode smoke: explicit --pc-start/--pc-end. ROI bounds come from
#    the $DUMP written in step 4 (csrwi 0x7C0,0/1 encodings: 7c005073 and
#    7c00d073; CSR name is "milmb" on Andes, raw encoding is stable).
if [ -s "${DUMP:-}" ]; then
  ENTER=$(awk 'matched==0 && /7c005073/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}' "$DUMP")
  EXIT=$(awk 'matched==0 && /7c00d073/{gsub(":","",$1); print $1; matched=1}' "$DUMP")
  if [ -n "${ENTER:-}" ] && [ -n "${EXIT:-}" ]; then
    KFILE3="$TMPDIR_ROOT/pc.kanata"
    set +e
    out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
            --mode pc --pc-start "0x$ENTER" --pc-end "0x$EXIT" \
            --kanata "$KFILE3" 2>&1); rc=$?
    set -e
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
    [ -s "$KFILE3" ] || fail "pc-mode: kanata file not created or empty"
    head -1 "$KFILE3" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
      || fail "pc-mode: missing Kanata header"
    grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE3" \
      || fail "pc-mode: no I records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE3")"
    ok "pc-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
  else
    echo "[skip] could not extract csrwi 0x7c0 markers from rt_c_hello"
  fi
fi

echo "PASS test_hsim_kanata"

echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--kanata"  || fail "run --help missing --kanata:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q -- "--objdump" || fail "run --help missing --objdump:\n$out"
ok "run --help lists --kanata and --objdump"

#    marker/pc).
set +e
out=$("$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode icount \
       --kanata "$TMPDIR_ROOT/x.kanata" 2>&1); rc=$?
set -e
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "--kanata with icount should rc=2, got $rc:\n$out"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "kanata" || fail "icount rejection should mention kanata:\n$out"
ok "--kanata + --mode icount rejected (rc=2)"

# 3. marker-mode smoke: kanata file is created, non-empty, has Kanata header.
KFILE="$TMPDIR_ROOT/marker.kanata"
SMOKE_TIMEOUT=60
set +e
out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
        --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE" 2>&1); rc=$?

grep -q "^R	" "$KFILE" \
  || fail "marker-mode: kanata file has no R (retire_insn) records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE")"

#    proves the OBJDUMP_FILE env reached vsim via e2e.sh.

OBJDUMP_TOOL="${OBJDUMP_TOOL:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"

          --mode marker --kanata "$KFILE2" --objdump "$DUMP" 2>&1); rc=$?

    KFILE3="$TMPDIR_ROOT/pc.kanata"
    set +e
    out=$(timeout "$SMOKE_TIMEOUT" "$HSIM" run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf \
            --mode pc --pc-start "0x$ENTER" --pc-end "0x$EXIT" \
            --kanata "$KFILE3" 2>&1); rc=$?
    set -e
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc-mode kanata run failed rc=$rc; output:\n$out"
    [ -s "$KFILE3" ] || fail "pc-mode: kanata file not created or empty"
    head -1 "$KFILE3" | grep -q "^Kanata" \
      || fail "pc-mode: missing Kanata header"
    grep -q "^I	" "$KFILE3" \
      || fail "pc-mode: no I records:\n$(head -20 "$KFILE3")"
    ok "pc-mode --kanata produces a valid kanata trace"
  else
    echo "[skip] could not extract csrwi 0x7c0 markers from rt_c_hello"
  fi
fi

echo "PASS test_hsim_kanata"

2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but with the QEMU2 leg removed those extra CSRs are no longer restored anywhere -- they remain in `hybrid_state_v1` only as the drained record. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 4 switching modes, split by what they profile.

Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):
- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for CSR-less workloads.
- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices (interval = insns per slice), cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate. Drive via `./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` (or the equivalent `./hsim.py estimate`) -- Python golden only until the C++ port lands. The bbv-profile / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.

`./andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc|icount` is the unified orchestrator (`./hsim.py run --mode simpoint` for SimPoint); `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.

```sh

- `--kanata` is only valid with `--model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium` or `--model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`. icount and
  simpoint modes have no single ROI-exit PC; they are rejected with
  rc=2.
- marker mode requires exactly one `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit marker) in the
  ELF. If the binary has more than one, vsim errors out with
  `multiple ... markers in ELF -- use --model hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium with explicit --pc-end`.
  Switch to pc mode and pick the desired exit explicitly.
- `--objdump` requires `--kanata`.

How it works:

- hsim forwards `KANATA_FILE` (and optionally `OBJDUMP_FILE`) to
  `tests/e2e.sh`, which appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` PC from CsrTrigger (marker mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only

  base 0 and shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run (the program dies in an
  illegal-instruction trap loop). Hybrid runs only survive it because the
  exit marker retires on vsim. Delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use
  `--trigger pc` instead (see `tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c`:
  `say_hello` / `vplat_roi_end`).

  its MMIO cost is real), but it still adds those UART cycles to the figure -
  keep measured kernels I/O-free when you care about clean numbers.

## 2. marker mode - the default (profiles a kernel)

### What it does

QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire
time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
same on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes
ax45mp, so the fixture binary embeds these two `csrwi` instructions at the
kernel boundaries. vsim's drain at the `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` marker is the
natural tail of the run.
